page: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v5 is a compute-oriented virtual machine belonging to the DLSv5 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 48 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, Geekbench multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU scores all placing in the top 25% tier. Memory performance is also robust, showing strong large-block read and write bandwidth alongside high Passmark memory scores. The server demonstrates high throughput in specialized tasks, achieving top-tier results in software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, image processing, and static web serving. Conversely, single-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the average range. Large-scale LLM inference, specifically text generation with a 70B model, represents a performance bottleneck, registering in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D64ls_v5 offers a high density of compute resources relative to its memory footprint, making it a viable option for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory allocations or local NVMe storage. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs reduces overhead for architectures relying on external network-attached storage. This hardware profile is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation pipelines, static web serving, and database operations that benefit from high multi-core throughput and strong memory bandwidth.
